title: Dispatch LTP 3: Averted Collision Leaves a Different Headline
summary: The next early edition changes after a driver refuses his scheduled route.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: The two streetcars did not collide on Saturday. Driver Alice Mercer kept her car at the depot as ordered. Shortly after the hour named in the advance report, its headline began to fade. Dr. Saye, Mr. Ashcombe, and this correspondent watched the words “TWO CARS STRIKE AT BELL LANE” give way to a report of a stalled car and delayed passengers.

No hand touched the page. Its ink remained dry. The revised account named Miss Mercer as the driver who refused the route. It also quoted a passenger complaining that the city had obeyed “a newspaper from nowhere.” That passenger made the same remark later in the afternoon.

The bundle dated 8 September arrived as usual this morning. It contains no streetcar report. Instead, it describes a fire in a warehouse off Narrow Street and says the building’s side door will be locked when workers try to leave. Inspector Daniel Voss has examined the warehouse and ordered the door unbolted.

Dr. Saye says the altered headline argues against a single fixed tomorrow. The pages may show a course that changes when people act on it. She cannot explain why the ink makes its correction before events finish unfolding.

Miss Mercer has asked the Chronicle to stop naming private citizens in the advance reports. “I made a choice any driver could make,” she told us. “Now people are watching me as though I know what will happen next.” Mr. Ashcombe says the early editions will remain in the office except where a direct warning is needed.
